title: Web-Based Simulator of Superscalar RISC-V Processors
problem: Students and professionals lack interactive tools to understand superscalar RISC-V processor architectures and their interaction with software. Traditional learning resources do not provide hands-on experience with processor design trade-offs and HPC optimization techniques.
motivation: Understanding processor architectures and HW/SW co-design is essential for developing fast and power-efficient programs.
method: The simulator lets you build a custom superscalar RISC-V processor (a processor design where multiple instructions execute in parallel) by adjusting architecture parameters like pipeline depth, instruction-per-cycle throughput, and cache sizes. You write C code and compile it within the tool, then the simulator runs your code on your custom processor design and records detailed timing measurements. By comparing results across different architecture choices, you can directly see how design decisions trade off against each other—for example, more parallelism increases speed but also power consumption and chip complexity.
key_novelty: A web-based simulator combining customizable superscalar RISC-V processor design with C programming support, so you can immediately see how architecture choices affect program performance.
contributions: Web-based GUI for RISC-V superscalar processor simulation
Customizable processor and memory architecture parameters
Full C compiler integration with detailed runtime statistics
Platform for teaching HW/SW co-design and HPC optimization
